details:
Add a new Blend Mode "Alpha Threshold", with a new shader parameter "Detail Threshold". Wherever the detail alpha is greater than "Detail Threshold", the detail color replaces the main color. Otherwise, the main color is used without modification.

Like all other detail blend modes, the geometry remains opaque. This means that this feature, and all of its usecases, should be available for use on Quest without performance issues.

Usecases:

 - Sharp-edged decals, such as stickers

 - Replacing cutout-based expressions on some avatars, such as pooltoy avatars.

   - I've already done this on a couple avatars using the alpha blended mode (or multiplyx2, before toon standard), but I can't cut resolution as much as I would like without making the edges of the expressions fuzzy.

 - 2D SDF-texture based text/graphics on quest avatars

   - I've not yet spotted any way to perform a threshold based on the contents of a texture using quest shaders. I could have missed something.

(I would likely make use of this to replicate an effect I've done on the PC version of my avatar, where the borders between every color are kept sharp using thresholding.)

Name Bikeshedding:

I don't particularly care about the final name, and will "Alpha Threshold" as a bikesheddable placeholder for now.

You could call this Cutout, or some variation thereof. "Cutout Overlay," perhaps?

Pro: It works the same way, but instead of discarding it uses the main color. Instant intuition for people already familiar with cutout transparency.

Con: I'm worried about confusion with cutout transparency, and people thinking that this enables transparency on quest (or, alternatively, dismissing it because transparency doesn't exist on quest.) This is why I've refrained from calling it cutout or making comparisons to cutout in the title or main body of the feature request.
title: Toon Standard "Alpha Threshold" detail blend mode
